name: Mizo

ancestors.notes: Mizo/Lushai is a Central Kuki-Chin (Kuki-Chin proper) language descended from Proto-Kuki-Chin (VanBik 2009).

notes: Mizo (Lushai), spoken in Mizoram, India. Central Kuki-Chin branch, Sino-Tibetan. Alphabet devised 1894 by J.H. Lorrain & F.W. Savidge on Hunterian transliteration principles and is highly regular/phonemic (Wikipedia; Lorrain 1940 grammar). Circumflex marks long vowels (aâ eê iî oô uû). ⟨ch chh⟩ spell the ALVEOLAR affricates /ts tsʰ/ and ⟨ṭ ṭh⟩ the flapped [t͡ɾ t͡ɾʰ] per the Wikipedia Mizo consonant table (corrected from an earlier postalveolar reading). ⟨aw⟩ ranges [o]~[ɔ] per the same table; /ɔ/ is used here. Digraph ⟨aw⟩ is the single spelling for the mid-back rounded vowel /ɔ/ -- earns its key because a+w does not compose to /ɔ/ under this spec's own a=/a/, w=/w/(not a standalone grapheme here) values, i.e. it is not a concatenation of independently-mapped parts. Digraphs ⟨ph th kh ch chh⟩ spell the aspirated stop/affricate series (single phonemes, AGENTS.md test 2). ⟨ng⟩ spells the velar nasal /ŋ/, a single segment not n+g. The pre-aspirated sonorants ⟨hm hn hng hl hr⟩ and post-aspirated ⟨ngh⟩ spell voiceless sonorants /m̥ n̥ ŋ̊ l̥ r̥/ -- single phonemes per Chhangte (1993) and Wikipedia's consonant table, not h+sonorant clusters, so each earns its key under AGENTS.md test 1/2. Mizo has 8 lexical tones/intonations realised on the vowel (Chhangte 1993; Weidert 1975) which the standard orthography largely leaves unmarked in ordinary text (only length is marked via circumflex); tone is therefore not represented in this grapheme map (would require diacritics absent from the citable orthographic norm) -- documented here rather than fabricated as extra vowel keys.
